name: dequal
oneLiner: Answers whether two JavaScript values are deeply equal.
problem: === compares references; developers need to know whether two structures hold the same data.

capabilities.name: Deep structural equality
capabilities.behavior: Returns true when two values have the same structure and contents: plain objects compare own keys and values recursively (key order ignored), arrays compare length and items in order, and values must share the same constructor. An array never equals a plain object.
edgeCases: An extra key on either side makes the values unequal.
Different constructors are unequal even with identical keys.

capabilities.name: Equality for built-in object types
capabilities.behavior: Dates are equal when they hold the same time; regular expressions when source and flags match; Maps and Sets when they have the same size and matching entries (Set order ignored, object keys found by deep equality); typed arrays, ArrayBuffers and DataViews when their bytes match.
capabilities.inputs: Dates, RegExps, Maps, Sets, binary views.

designIdeas: A single predicate with no options.
Constructor identity is part of equality.
A 'lite' variant trades built-in type support for size.
limitations: Answers only yes or no; it cannot say what differs.
